Mesh Action

By: Tebadi Mmotla | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South African women take big Pharmaceutical company Johnson and Jonson to court over mesh defects

Unique Selling Point:
Multi-billion dollar pharmaceutical giant, Johnson and Johnson faces yet another class-action lawsuit for manufacturing and distributing mesh defects. This time the lawsuit is brought forth by South Africa women.

The tale is told by two women from different parts of the country, who came together after realizing they have one common enemy. Through social media and other means of communication, they discovered that they are experiencing similar health complications.

They all started experiencing these complications after undergoing an operation where transvaginal mesh was used. Their lives changed forever.

They are now part of a class-action lawsuit aiming to make the big pharma pay for concealing evidence about the mesh defects.


Summary:
In October last year, a class-action lawsuit was filed at the Johannesburg High Court against Johnson and Johnson, for manufacturing, and selling transvaginal mesh devices used in health facilities across the country.

These women claim that the mesh which was used when they underwent operations to treat either dislocated pelvic organs or urine problems had defects and was not properly tested.

Transvaginal mesh like other mesh products, is made from polypropylene.

Polypropylene is simply described as a plastic that is soft and flexible. When the mesh which contains this polypropylene is implanted in the pelvic area it causes complications in some women. This is because the muscle in the pelvic area is thin, and struggles to accommodate the mesh.

This triggers foreign body reaction. The body identifies the mesh as a foreign body. As a result, the body fights the mesh, and the mesh starts to break down into pieces, and folds itself, causing erosion or failure.

It is this erosion that causes constant pain in the pelvic area. This is why the mesh is labeled as a defect.

The applicants claim that Johnson and Johnson was aware of these defects, and failed to implement measures to protect the safety of women. Therefore the company is liable for the suffering, income loss and the psychiatric injuries they suffered due to the faulty mesh.
Johnson and Johnson is accused of providing misleading information about the safety and the effectiveness of these meshes, and continued to manufacture, market, and distribute the mesh implants.







Further information:
In 2022 Women in Australia saw victory in a landmark ruling when Johnson and Johnson settled for A$300m in two separate lawsuits. The first lawsuit in 2020, and the second lawsuit was filed in 2021 for women who were not eligible to be part of the first lawsuit as their meshes were implanted after 04 July 2017.

In 2016 in the U.S, the state of California sued Johnson and Johnson, along with its subsidiary company Ethicon for concealing the defects of pelvic meshes, which resulted in women experiencing serious health complications. The company was ordered to pay $302 million.

Jonhson and Johnson petitioned the Supreme Court for a review. On February 21, (2023) The U.S Supreme Court of Appeal dismissed Johnson and Johnson’s appeal.

In 2008 Drug and Food Administration [FDA] in the U.S issued a notification warning that there might be possible risks that might occur when a pelvic mesh is implanted. In 2018 the federal agency ordered manufacturing companies of transvaginal mesh to stop selling and distributing the products.

In South Africa, the Health Products Regulatory Authority has not issued a warning. Will these women see the same victory as those abroad?

Script:


MESH ACTION


MUSIC TRACK

VISUALS: A hospital entry, and different TVT meshes

INTRO SEQUENCE/TEASER SUMMARY OF STORY

1 VO: It’s a medical device that’s been around for over 2 decades.

VISUALS: A collage of class-action lawsuits on mesh defects

2 VO: …now in the middle of endless lawsuits as women all over the world take big pharma to court.

VISUALS: Johannesburg High Court

3 VO: In South Africa a legal storm is brewing…

UPSOUND HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF: Maybe there’s other people out there also with the same problem that doesn’t know about it.

4 VO: …as women gear up to take the manufacturer's court…

UPSOUND CHANTELL 27:56 to 29:04: I couldn't understand why all those things are even on the market.

5 VO: …the device is faulty they say…and damaged them, for life.

UPSOUND ZAIN 10:43: This is a case about a manufacturer who's not disclosing the risks and all the information required so that surgeons and patients can make the right decisions for the patient.

DIP TO BLACK

ACT 1


Visual: Masa and Hanlie into the house

6 VO: Hanlie Ryan is an avid cyclist…

UPS…Your mind can go… you can think of everything…

Visual: FX6_1102.MXF FX6_1103.MXF FX6_1104_MXF FX6_1105.MXF /
Johanna Hanlie puts on her cycling gear, and cycles outside.

7 VO: She’s spent years building up her amateur ranking…but for the last few years…her dreams of competing professionally have slowly been slipping out of her reach.

Visual: Sipping coffee..

8 VO: Hanlie has been living in the aftermath of a medical procedure that up-ended her life.. It started 12 years ago.

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 02:00 I started realizing that I'm getting infections, a bladder infection, and a urinary infection, and I couldn't understand why I had a problem. Like you go and then like 10 minutes later you have to go again.

09 VO: The doctor diagnosed bladder prolapse - one of a number of conditions that can develop when organs in the pelvic area drop or collapse.

MASA A7SIII_8686.MP4 03:29 to 03:30: And what did he tell you can help?

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 03:31 to 03:49: All you do is you put the mesh in. A sling in, he called it this mesh, he says, and then you pull it up and you'll be able to urinate properly.

10 VO: But for Hanlie the mesh caused incredible pain and discomfort...at the worst possible time, just as she was about to embark on a new relationship.

MASA A7SIII_8686.MP4 04:04 04:06: Did you know any pros and cons of this?

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 04:07 to 04:08: No

MASA A7SIII_8686.MP4 04:09 to 04:12: You were just told that this is gonna fix you

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 04:12 to: 04:29 : You trust the gynecologist. I've been with him. He knows my body. So if he says that's the thing to go for, you just
believe in it.

11 VO: But what is a mesh device, and what’s it used for?

When pelvic muscles weaken, organs like the uterus and bladder can drop and press into the vagina… causing problems like urine leakage. Living a normal life can become impossible.

Mesh is used to bind up and lift the organs..

Prof Shingai Mutambirwa is the head of Urology at George Mukhari Academic Hospital, and Sefako Makgatho Health Sciences University.

PROF MUTAMBIRWA FX3_8433.MP4 00:47 to 01:22: The biggest issue with meshes is that they were actually developed over 20, 30 years ago for a number of reasons

12 VO: Mesh contains the plastic “polypropylene” and comes in different shapes and sizes..Hanlie got what’s called a transvaginal mesh…an operation through the vagina.

Visual: implanting a mesh

PROF MUTAMBIRWA FX3_8433.MP4 04:27: There's essentially only two layers in the vagina. There's the skin and a little bit of muscle. So obviously it's a much thinner area to put a mesh in.

13 VO: While these implants had a high success rate in the short term.. more and more women reacted badly in the long term...what science calls the phase four trial.. doctors were none the wiser…and kept on with the implants…

PROF MUTAMBIRWA FX3_8433.MP4

And although the trials were done and they did show the outcomes were good. The problem was that especially when we're doing what we call phase four trials, where people start looking at the side effect per long-term side effect profile, there was a significant increase in the amount of side effects, and the main ones would be erosion because the skin is so thin that it comes out.

VISUAL & A graphic of mesh devices.
https://www.jnjmedtech.com/en-US/company/ethicon/all-products?items_per_page=20&jnjmdc_product_category_ref_target_id[3051]=3051

14 VO: The big problem is that the mesh dis-integrates in the body, causing even more pain for some women.

VISUAL: FX6_1213.MXF FX6_1215.MXF A doctor taking a pair of scissors.

VISUAL: A graphic showing the Gynecare TVT Abbrevo mesh.

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 04:32 to 05:07: Discomfort after the operation, but you think it's supposed to be like that. Then you try to recover. They say, you know, a certain amount of time you get better. But I never felt better.

15 VO: Outrageously, when Hanlie complained to her doctor, he said it was psychological…even though sexual intercourse became impossible.

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 08:20: It was uncomfortable to have a full-on intimate relationship…But I thought, you know, Maybe it's because of the new relationship. And that's when I went back to the doctor, to my gynae …, he said to me, there's nothing wrong with you. It's all in your imagination.

MASA FX3_8433.Mp4 07:42 to 07:45: did you know at the time that this was because of the mesh?

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 07:47 to 08:01: No.

VISUAL: Timeline of transvaginal mesh in the USA

ACT 2

16 VO: And it’s here that Hanlie’s story and - as she would discover - those of many other women - takes a dramatic turn: As far back as 2008… the American Food and Drug Administration issued repeated safety warnings about transvaginal mesh.

After $8 billion was paid out to some 100,000 women who suffered complications…. the FDA – in 2019 – put a stop to the manufacturing of transvaginal mesh for pelvic prolapse in the US.

17 VO: The manufacturer of the defective mesh products, Johnson & Johnson, has been sued in many countries in the last decade.

UPSOUND LINK MASA FX3_8371 LINK: hundreds of women across the world have taken this big pharma to court. And they have won.

VISUALS: Articles on the Australian and American victory.

18 VO: In 2019, the Federal Court of Australia found that J&J’s transvaginal mesh hadn’t been sufficiently evaluated, and carried great risks.

In the United States, a Philadelphia jury ordered J&J to pay over $100 million to a woman who suffered injuries due to the transvaginal mesh.

So why were these products still available to South African women?

VISUAL: SAHPRA website

19 VO: The Health Products Regulatory Authority declined an interview to tell us. In a written statement SAHPRA said they engaged with companies with mesh products, and that those who still market mesh products were subject to SAHPRA regulations.

VISUAL DJI_0002.MP4: Aerial establisher Welkom Free State

MASA FX3_8319.MP4 03:41 to 03:45: Did your doctor explain to you what your options were after diagnosing?

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF 03:46 to 04:56: It was either hysterectomy or let's lift your uterus.

VISUAL: Chantell sitting down and holding her medication

20 VO: In 2017 Chantell Bothma gave birth to a baby boy and suffered a prolapsed uterus.

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF So because I was still young, he said that we have to preserve my uterus. So I thought, great. You know, there's a solution for my problem. I can still decide on whether I want to expand my family. So I said, yes, you know, let's do it.

UPSOUND FX6_1198

21 VO: But for Chantell there was more in store.

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF08:10 Now that the uterus was lifted, they could see, my bladder also moved …. So then of course they said, we'll, we'll fix it the same way.

MASA FX3_8319.MP409:12 to 09:13: So you have to go for another operation.

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF09:13 to 10:24: Yes..Then after that, everything got worse.

22 VO: In debilitating pain, Chantell was in and out of doctor's rooms… losing precious time with her new baby.

VISUAL: Chantell and her son

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF 13:12 and 15:05 I couldn't pick him up. If I wanted to pick him up, somebody had to pick him up and give him to me. just thinking about everything I missed out on and not being able to be a normal mom. It was hard.

23 VO: A SPECIALIST finally advised Chantell to have it taken out - although it’s even more painful to remove mesh from the tissue once it’s embedded.

VISUAL: Chantell and masa walk into a building

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF17:34: I said fine, let's go ahead with it. Remove it. And with that I had to have a hysterectomy.

MASA FX3_8319.MP318:43 to 18:46: And after these procedures to try and rectify how are you feeling?

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF18:37: Okay, so after the uterus mesh was taken out, Masa, I felt an immediate relief in this area and my lower back. It was like something was pulling and it just snapped.

VISUAL: Hanlie on the computer

24 VO: Seeking solace AND SUPPORT online, Chantell and Hanlie… found a number of other women, and the courage … to join forces to sue the companies at the root of their pain.

ACT 3

MASA FX3_8319.MP427:52 to 27:55: Who would you say you blame for all of this?

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF 27:56: It's definitely the people that put the product on the market. I can't blame the doctors, they advise you on what's available out there.

MASA LINK FX3_8432: Listening to these women's stories really broke my heart when I think about the cost of it all, and I'm not just talking financially, I mean a first time mom not being able to spend precious moments with their infant hanley's plight of lack of intimacy and companionship, the loneliness and the rejection, not forgetting the physical pain.

VISUAL: outside J&J

25 VO: The first company to be served in a class action suit is Johnson and Johnson South Africa. Nine women have joined the suit. Zain Lundell is a class action specialist.

VISUAL FX3_8454.MP4 Masa walking with Zain at the Johannesburg Court

ZAIN FX6_1233.MXF03:28 to 04:47: Our position, and based on the documents we've reviewed…mesh manufacturers knew of the significant risk associated with these products.

MASA FX3_84443.MP4 04:47 to 04:52 : What makes you say that Johnson and Johnson knew about these defects but ignored them anyway?

ZAIN FX6_1233.MXF04:52 to 05:51: Certain transvaginal mesh products, basically were taken off the market in the United States. Few years ago, those mesh products were still sold in other countries.

VISUALS FX3_8382.MP4 Outside Johnson and Johnson

26 VO: We contacted Johnson & Johnson for an interview and they declined. They say they were notified of the claims over a year ago. They requested claimants’ medical records but haven’t received anything yet.

27: They add that the mesh is a device prescribed after consultation with a surgeon. They claim that the risks associated with these devices are properly identified in the products’ “Instructions for Use”…

28 VO: But if Hanlie and Chantell have their way, the company will have to explain … …and pay up.

CHANTELL FX6_1016.MXF

I could have these things removed out of my body.

I had a medical aid. I was lucky enough they approved the procedures, but there are women out there that can't afford it. They don't have medical aid.

VISUALFX6_1080 TO FX_1095 Hanlie with her dogs.

29 VO: Hanlie’s medical aid insists the surgery to remove the mesh is cosmetic and won’t cover the costs. So, she has little choice but to live with the consequences.

JOHANNA HANLIE FX6_1094.MXF 20:50: People start wondering why she is alone? She's never with somebody, what's wrong with it? But you learn to live with it. You make the best of it. I've got so many friends, but the loneliness, that's why I got my two dogs. They are my everything.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): South African women take big Pharmaceutical company Johnson and Jonson to court over mesh defects
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Multi-billion dollar pharmaceutical giant, Johnson and Johnson faces yet another class-action lawsuit for manufacturing and distributing mesh defects. This time the lawsuit is brought forth by South Africa women. The tale is told by two women from different parts of the country, who came together after realizing they have one common enemy. Through social media and other means of communication, they discovered that they are experiencing similar health complications. They all started experiencing these complications after undergoing an operation where transvaginal mesh was used. Their lives changed forever. They are now part of a class-action lawsuit aiming to make the big pharma pay for concealing evidence about the mesh defects.
metadata.Summary: In October last year, a class-action lawsuit was filed at the Johannesburg High Court against Johnson and Johnson, for manufacturing, and selling transvaginal mesh devices used in health facilities across the country. These women claim that the mesh which was used when they underwent operations to treat either dislocated pelvic organs or urine problems had defects and was not properly tested. Transvaginal mesh like other mesh products, is made from polypropylene. Polypropylene is simply described as a plastic that is soft and flexible. When the mesh which contains this polypropylene is implanted in the pelvic area it causes complications in some women. This is because the muscle in the pelvic area is thin, and struggles to accommodate the mesh. This triggers foreign body reaction. The body identifies the mesh as a foreign body. As a result, the body fights the mesh, and the mesh starts to break down into pieces, and folds itself, causing erosion or failure. It is this erosion that causes constant pain in the pelvic area. This is why the mesh is labeled as a defect. The applicants claim that Johnson and Johnson was aware of these defects, and failed to implement measures to protect the safety of women. Therefore the company is liable for the suffering, income loss and the psychiatric injuries they suffered due to the faulty mesh. Johnson and Johnson is accused of providing misleading information about the safety and the effectiveness of these meshes, and continued to manufacture, market, and distribute the mesh implants.
metadata.Further information: In 2022 Women in Australia saw victory in a landmark ruling when Johnson and Johnson settled for A$300m in two separate lawsuits. The first lawsuit in 2020, and the second lawsuit was filed in 2021 for women who were not eligible to be part of the first lawsuit as their meshes were implanted after 04 July 2017. In 2016 in the U.S, the state of California sued Johnson and Johnson, along with its subsidiary company Ethicon for concealing the defects of pelvic meshes, which resulted in women experiencing serious health complications. The company was ordered to pay $302 million. Jonhson and Johnson petitioned the Supreme Court for a review. On February 21, (2023) The U.S Supreme Court of Appeal dismissed Johnson and Johnson’s appeal. In 2008 Drug and Food Administration [FDA] in the U.S issued a notification warning that there might be possible risks that might occur when a pelvic mesh is implanted. In 2018 the federal agency ordered manufacturing companies of transvaginal mesh to stop selling and distributing the products. In South Africa, the Health Products Regulatory Authority has not issued a warning. Will these women see the same victory as those abroad?
